parameters.content:
## 🧭 People Trace + Relocation Timeline — Searchbug (api_trace)

Locate a person and reconstruct **where they have lived, in what order, and for how long** — from whatever you know: SSN, name, or address. One person at a time or a whole CSV. The workflow auto-picks the strongest search method available for each row.

### How it works
1. **Single:** enter what you know (REF optional). **Bulk:** leave the fields blank and upload a CSV (first_name, middle_name, last_name, address, city, state, ssn, ref).
2. Detect Search Type picks the strongest method per row; Build API Params shapes the request; Dedupe Subjects drops repeat rows so the same person is never traced twice.
3. The API call retries 3× and is throttled to 1 request/second. Rows with nothing usable are saved as SKIPPED instead of failing the run.
4. Flatten Records makes one row per address. Build Relocation Timeline then sorts each person's addresses oldest-first and derives:
   • **MOVE_SEQUENCE** — the order they lived there, 1 = earliest on file
   • **IS_CURRENT** — the address seen most recently
   • **MONTHS_AT_ADDRESS** and **YEARS_SINCE_LAST_SEEN**
   • **MOVED_STATE** — did this move cross a state line?
   • **NAME_MATCH_SCORE 0–100** — does the traced person match the name searched?
   • **FLAGS** — CURRENT_ADDRESS, RECENT_MOVE, OUT_OF_STATE_MOVE, SHORT_STAY, LONG_TERM, NO_DATES, WEAK_NAME_MATCH
5. Two sheets are written:
   • **People Trace** — one row per address (37 columns)
   • **PT Summary** — one row per person: current address, states lived in, years traced, move count, average months per address, and a HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW mobility tier.

### How to set up
- [ ] Add your Searchbug CO_CODE + PASS in the People Trace API node (Body Parameters)
- [ ] Connect your OWN Google Sheets account in BOTH Save nodes
- [ ] Point them at your own spreadsheet and create two tabs:
      • "People Trace" (37 columns — see Save Trace Detail)
      • "PT Summary" (20 columns — see Save Trace Summary)
- [ ] Activate and share the form link

### Search priority
SSN → Address+City+State → First+Last+City+State → First+Last+State → First+Last → SKIPPED

### 🔒 Privacy
Only the LAST 4 digits of the SSN are saved (ssn_last4) — the full SSN is never written to the sheet. This returns real people's address histories: keep the destination sheet access-controlled, and do not use it for FCRA-covered decisions (employment, tenancy, credit, insurance).

## 1. Single or Bulk Input

Single or Bulk? checks whether any single field was filled. If yes → Normalize Input; if all blank → Extract CSV first.

Normalize Input standardizes the column names so both paths share one schema — first_name / First Name / FIRST_NAME / fname all work, and ssn also accepts social.

## 2. Detect & Build

Detect Search Type auto-picks the strongest method available for each row: an SSN beats an address, an address beats a name, and a fuller name beats a sparser one.

Build API Params shapes the request for the chosen method — deliberately blanking the fields that method does not use, so a half-filled row cannot send a contradictory query.

## 3. Dedupe, Search & Flatten

Dedupe Subjects collapses repeat rows into one trace and stamps each person with a SUBJECT_ID that follows them into both sheets.

Has Search Fields? routes rows with nothing usable to Skipped Row — they still reach the sheet, marked SKIPPED, so a bad CSV row is visible instead of silently missing.

The API node retries 3× and sends 1 request per second. Attach Subject Context carries the SUBJECT_ID past the call, and Flatten Records makes one row per address, handling the single-record object, the multi-record array, API errors and empty results.

## 4. Build the Timeline

Build Relocation Timeline is what makes this more than a lookup. Per person it sorts the addresses oldest-first and works out the move order, how long each address lasted, which one is current, whether each move crossed a state line, and how well the traced name matches the one searched.

This is the part a plain HTTP Request node cannot do: the API returns a bag of addresses, and this turns it into a history.

## ⚠️ 5. Two Outputs

**Save Trace Detail** — one row per address, 37 columns: the 11 timeline fields first, then the 26 original trace fields.

**Save Trace Summary** — one row per person: current address and since when, every state lived in, years traced, move count, out-of-state moves, average months per address, mobility tier, and all phones found.

Connect your OWN Google Sheets credential in both and create the tabs with matching row-1 headers.

Don't click ⋮ → Refresh — it erases the column mapping.

Privacy: only ssn_last4 is stored. Keep the sheet access-controlled.
